chat.author: Jeffrey Haas

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: Perversely, does BMP reach "maturity" when the versions stop going up and the extensions continue - like bgp - or is it better to continue bumping version numbers?

chat.text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/statement-iesg-on-design-teams-20011221/

chat.author: Mukul Srivastava
chat.text: Many times running code may not be possible because the draft may still be in churn. How should such cases be handled ?

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The primary challenge for counters is getting everyone to agree what is being counted.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: As an example, for the current presentation, these counters are already present in rfc 4273 in the mib in some cases. These are good adds - but making sure the documentation for the counter says "these should be the same" is important.

chat.author: Ahmed Elhassany
chat.text: We yet haven't standardized that many extension (despite the many proposals) to say we need up a cleanup version to merge them into one standard protocol. And, it's not clear to me: what is not possible with another BMPv4 extension that requires a new protocol version.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: TLV is getting us there!  I mostly nod toward the fact that bgp has been version 4 for most of my time doing networking in the 90s.

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: Just to make sure I understand, this proposal is on top of BMPv4 (ietf-grow-bmp-tlv is not a normative reference). Disclaimer: still have to read the draft

chat.text: Copying an aside conversation I had with Camilo, nothing stops grow from specifying a given set of BGP statistics BOTH in BMP and YANG at the same time if that's the WG's like.  Right now we have ships in the night due to the YANG not yet being shipped - but we're finishing AD comments on it.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text:
Maxence Younsi said:

Oh and was not aware of the bgp mib v2. I will have a look, thanks for the ref

I would take inspiration from the bgp yang model.  MIBv2 didn't make it out of early enterprise implementation.  The WG requirements thrashed too much and we gave up.  We also figured out that much of the structured state couldn't be represented in SMIv2 language for MIBS

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: The failures for the BGP MIBv2 project was the death knell for MIBs.  And also the lie that YANG was ready to take over the work at that point.  It's taken a while.

chat.author: Ahmed Elhassany
chat.text: I agree with Job, all points are sound. However, one negative side effect for pushing vendors to provide early closed source implementation, they will implement the -03 of the draft while the draft is progresses to IESG at version -21. That has two implications. First on IETF, do we still have an implementation?. Second, on operators, usually means for years we will have to deal with multiple pre-draft implementations in the wild.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text: What you do as a vendor vs. specs that are moving targets is very messy.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text:
Always relevant vs. Job's presentation:
https://datatracker.ietf.org/meeting/97/materials/slides-97-idr-code-point-management-02

chat.author: Thomas Graf
chat.text:
As information, as BPM co-chair, we reached out to the working group mailing list and asked: https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/ippm/OaHSR7HYD0KUFNaY9ePWrIbKTew/ and reached consensus on: 
The WG requires an implementation for standard track documents. In some cases exceptions can be applied. Whenever such an exception applies, the exception justification must be included in the specification document or its write-up.
However, at IESG, we received push back on ambiguity and therefore we are driving now:
The WG prioritizes documents with implementations.

chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text:
For implementation status: 
https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc7942
